Many APIs support a `fields=` comma‑separated list or a projection object. | `&fields=id,createdAt,userId,status` | | 4️⃣ Handle Pagination | Large result sets usually come back paginated. # pseudo‑code example
token=None\nwhile True:\n resp = requests.get(url, params={\n \"sourceDomain\": \"downloads.com\",\n \"fields\": \"id,createdAt\",
\t\"pageToken\": token,\n }, headers=headers)\n data = resp.json()\n process(data[\"items\"])\n token = data.get(\"nextPageToken\")\n if not token:\n break\n``` | 5️⃣ Error Handling | Check status codes (200 OK vs 429 Too Many Requests, 401 Unauthorized, etc.). Retry after the time indicated in `Retry‑After`. | `if resp.status_code == 429:` … | --- ### Example Using cURL ```bash curl -H "X-Api-Key: dload_key" \ "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/files?sourceDomain=downloads.com&fields=id,metadata" ``` This call will return JSON something like: ```json { "items": [ { "id":"abc123", "metadata":{"size":102400,"format":"pdf"} }, { "id":"def456", "metadata":{"size":204800,"format":"zip"} } ], "nextPageToken":"XYZ789" } ``` Just iterate over all pages to collect every ID. --- #### Quick Checklist Before You Run It 1. **Endpoint URL** – Confirm the base path (`v1/files`, `/listDownloads`, etc.). 2. **Auth Header Name** – Some providers use `Authorization: Bearer ` instead of `X‑Api‑Key`. 3. **Query Parameter Names** – Verify names for filtering (`sourceDomain`, `fromDomain`, `site`, etc.) and field selection (`fields`, `projection`, `select`). 4. **Rate Limits & Quotas** – Respect them; add exponential backoff if needed. 5. **Data Privacy** – Never log raw responses containing sensitive identifiers unless absolutely necessary.
